recipes.name: Blue Cheese Dressing
ingredients: 120g / 3 oz Roquefort, or other creamy blue cheese (- about 1 lightly packed cup when crumbled (Note 1))
1/2 cup buttermilk (, plus more as needed (Note 3 for substitute))
2 tsp apple cider vinegar (, or lemon juice)
1/2 tsp Worcestershire sauce ((good to add if using mild flavoured blue cheese))
instructions: Mash - Put the blue cheese in a bowl and mash with a fork until it's crumbly (blue cheese is soft so it's easy).

Whisk - Add the remaining ingredients and whisk vigorously for about 15 seconds so the blue cheese blends in. There will be some little lumps - this is normal. Desirable! Lovely little pops of blue cheese (for completely smooth, see Note 4 ).
Thickness - This dressing is pretty thick, ideal for dipping, and clings well to leafy greens. To loosen, add a little bit more buttermilk.

page_recipe_notes: Recipe Notes: 1. Blue cheese – Use a creamy or semi-soft, full-flavoured blue cheese, here’s a list of common ones from the strongest to mildest: Roquefort – Sharp, tangy, salty, and complex *My favourite!* Stilton – strong, rich and savoury, but rounder and less sharp than Roquefort. Danish Blue / Danablu – classic blue-cheese flavour *good value easy-to-find choice* Gorgonzola Piccante – fairly strong and spicy, though creamier and less salty. Bleu d’Auvergne – medium-strong, creamy and earthy. Gorgonzola Dolce – mild, creamy, sweet and buttery with gentle blue flavour. Blue Castello – Most mild, good one for beginners! *good value, easy-to-find choice* Avoid very firm, dry blue cheeses as they don’t blend into the dressing as nicely. 2. Whole-egg mayonnaise – Whole egg mayo is creamier and less tangy than normal mayo. My recommended is S&W (Australia), followed by Hellman’s and Kewpie (equal second). 3. Buttermilk – S ubstitute 50/50 milk and yogurt, near identical consistency and flavour (tweak if needed eg if your yogurt is very thick or very thin). 4. For completely smooth dressing, blitz everything except the sour cream with a stick blender, then stir the sour cream in. Leftovers will keep for the shorter of the shelf life of the ingredients used. Nutrition for whole batch.
